newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end higher, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end higher, seen consolidating.

text.p: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) powered Bombay shares to a strong close on Wednesday helped by increasing transparency in company operations, brokers said.
"To a great extent freer information of current year workings is drawing fund managers," said S. Ramakrishnan, chief dealer at ASK-Raymond James Securities. "It is boosting confidence."
Some firms began releasing first quarter results for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) and traders expect other companies to follow. Indian firms do not usually unveil quarterly results.
Truck-maker TELCO fell 3.0 rupees to 388.50 on news that its first quarter sales has fallen more than 10 percent.
Traders said the decline was lower than the industry average of about 18 percent.
"FIIs were accumulating in the stock," Ramakrishnan said.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange index ended 23.97 points, or 0.57 percent, higher at a provisional 4,241.55.
Broker Sunil Kothari said the market was helped by fading political worries.
"Laloo (Prasad Yadav) is inside; the market is going up," he said, referring to the scandal-marred politician who on Wednesday surrendered to federal police.
Traders said they expect the market to consolidate in a 4,000-4,400 points range over the next three months.
"The market will consolidate at these levels until we have a clearer picture of the monsoon and first half results," one dealer at a foreign brokerage said.
The CRISIL-500 index gained 4.46 points to 789.61 and the MidCap-200 index firmed 5.15 to 529.40.
